framing: A theorem eliminates candidates, not open problems: a candidate is a proposed answer or design that commits to quantities the theorem forbids. Three states: eliminated (the violated relation with the numbers, kernel-checked where marked), consistent (not ruled out by these theorems; never "feasible"), cannot-rule (a required input or assumption is missing). An elimination holds only under the law's own assumptions, listed per constraint; three of the four original statements were judged narrower in scope than their claims by the assessor, and a candidate eliminated by a narrower statement is eliminated only under that statement's assumptions.
nextConstraint: Strength (R7), bending (R9), general allometry, climb, glide range with ground effect, the aerobic power bound (Fick) with the crossover size limit, and five genotype-level checks (the genetic code, pleiotropy closure, developmental ordering, the substitution-time budget and Haldane's cost) are formalised. Not yet formalised: elastic similarity, gill O2 uptake as a function of water O2 and gill area (the first link of the simulator chain), taxiing thrust from the caudal fin, aspect ratio and induced drag, the walking (pendulum) route of thompson1917-ch02-10, and any quantitative muscle-power law (R6 is carried only as a named hypothesis).

assumptions.neutral_wright_fisher: strictly neutral mutations, constant population size, Wright-Fisher reproduction, independent mutant fates (lean/Delphi/Kimura.lean header)
assumptions.wright_fisher_selection: Wright-Fisher sampling with relative fitness 1+s for the mutant, s constant (lean/Delphi/Favored.lean header)
assumptions.independent_fates_definition: the expected count is Kimura's definition rate x generations: independent fates, constant M, mu and s, no linkage (lean/Delphi/Favored.lean header)
assumptions.fixed_fitnesses_one_locus: one haploid or clonal locus, fixed fitnesses within the step, infinite population, no mutation (lean/Delphi/Fisher.lean header)
assumptions.equal_fecundity_1to1: equal fecundity of sexual and asexual females, a 1:1 sex ratio, males contributing nothing, discrete generations (lean/Delphi/MaynardSmith.lean header)
assumptions.isometric_constant_density: the same body family scaled without change of shape or density, so W = k L^3 (lean/Delphi/Thompson.lean header)
assumptions.isometric_areas: the area in question (lifting area, load-bearing cross-section, exchange surface) scales as k L^2 across the family (AreaLaw, lean/Delphi/Scaling.lean)
assumptions.same_material: the breaking stress σ is the same for every member of the family (R7)
assumptions.axial_loading: the member fails under axial load σ A; bending is not formalised
assumptions.lift_supported_flight: steady flight with lift ½ ρ v² S C_L equal to weight and 0 < C_L ≤ C_L,max (R4)
assumptions.constant_lift_coefficient_max_and_densit: C_L,max and ρ the same for every member of the family (R4 scaling)
assumptions.constant_lift_to_drag: L/D the same for every member and flight at v_min (R5)
assumptions.muscle_power_premise: Thompson's premise, contested: muscle mass a constant fraction f of body mass and mass-specific power p constant (R6, MusclePowerLaw)
assumptions.equal_froude_number: the compared animals move at equal Froude number v²/(g L) (R8)
assumptions.linear_elastic_slender_beam: Euler-Bernoulli beam: σ_b = M_b / Z with M_b = F ℓ, static load (R9)
assumptions.similar_sections: geometrically similar cross-sections, Z = k_Z d^3 with d ∝ L (R9)
assumptions.lever_arm_proportional: the lever arm ℓ scales as L (R9)
assumptions.body_like_load: the transverse load scales as the body, F ∝ L^3 (R9a; isometric mass with constant density)
assumptions.sheet_like_load: the transverse load is a lamina of constant thickness, F ∝ L^2 (R9b)
assumptions.power_law_forms: weight and lifting area each follow a single power law in L over the range in question (PowerLaw)
assumptions.power_balance_nonneg_losses: available mechanical power = level-flight power + W × climb rate + non-negative losses
assumptions.steady_unpowered_glide: one steady glide, no thrust, lift equal to weight, L/D ≤ (L/D)max, potential energy spent on drag work plus non-negative losses; ground effect only as a stated drag reduction
assumptions.fitted_mass_exponent_band: empirical entry E2: the mass exponent of a fitted field study lies in [2.90, 3.02] (six fitted rows of five species, the male-only outlier excluded and named); the candidate accepts the observation
assumptions.teleost_measured_ranges: empirical entry E3: efficiency, oxycaloric equivalent, cardiac output and arterial O2 content lie inside the measured teleost ranges the physiology chain cites, so the sustained aerobic ceiling at 0.06 kg is at most 0.0458 W
assumptions.no_aerial_uptake: empirical entry E4: gills do not ventilate in air, so airborne aerobic work is paid out of the O2 store carried into the air
assumptions.lethality_before_scoring: empirical entry E7: an animal that the source reports dead at or before the scoring stage cannot show the scored phenotype
assumptions.fick_aerobic_supply: sustained mechanical power ≤ η × E_O2 × Q × (Ca − Cv) with 0 ≤ Cv ≤ Ca, 0 ≤ η ≤ 1 (Fick; aerobic, not burst)
assumptions.standard_genetic_code: the standard genetic code as tabulated in lean/Delphi/Genotype.lean (no alternative or mitochondrial code, no selenocysteine, no editing); one codon per amino acid position
assumptions.map_links_are_the_gene_reach: the nodes the genotype map links a gene to are the nodes an edit to that gene may change; the map records links, not dynamics, so this bounds what a picture may hide, never how much a node changes
assumptions.zfin_stage_order: the ZFIN stage-series ids order the stages of development (they are assigned in developmental order for the main series), and develops_from means the derivative appears no earlier than its precursor
assumptions.independent_sequential_fixations: the required substitutions fix one after another at Kimura's rate M μ u with constant M, μ and u, 1/M ≤ u ≤ 1 (neutral or favoured, by the Favored module); no linkage, no standing variation, no recombination of partial solutions
assumptions.haldane_cost_of_selection: Haldane 1957's accounting: substitutions by selection over T generations are at most e T / c, with reproductive excess e and cost per substitution c. A contested model, carried as a named hypothesis and never proved here
assumptions.thermal_window_q10: lean/Delphi/Perturb.lean ThermalPerformance: sustained power is zero outside [CTmin, CTmax] (thermal performance curve, Schulte 2015) and at most P_ref Q10^((T - T_ref)/10) inside (Q10 rule; Rome et al. 1992: 1.88 for scup red-muscle power); body temperature equals water temperature
assumptions.station_holding_drag_fick: lean/Delphi/Perturb.lean SwimLimits: ground speed U_swim - U_current >= 0, sustained swimming <= U_crit (Plaut 2001), drag power ρ_w C_d A U^3 / 2 paid by sustained aerobic power (Fick bound of Flight.lean); burst swimming outside the model
assumptions.boyle_closed_bladder: lean/Delphi/Perturb.lean Hydrostatic + Boyle: absolute pressure 1 atm + 0.1 atm/m (Yancey 2020), closed bladder (no gas secreted or absorbed), fixed temperature, quasi-static (Kerr et al. 2023: fails for fast decompression)
assumptions.osmolyte_depth_cap: lean/Delphi/Perturb.lean OsmolyteDepthCap: teleost internal osmolality rises linearly with depth (TMAO) and cannot exceed seawater's; the isosmotic depth is at most 8200 m (Yancey et al. 2014, a prediction by extrapolation). Teleosts only
assumptions.isa_troposphere: lean/Delphi/Perturb.lean ISATroposphere: ρ(h) = ρ0 (1 - β h/T0)^n with ρ0 = 1.225 kg/m^3, T0 = 288.15 K, β = 0.0065 K/m (Narayanan and Osechas 2022), n = g0/(R_d β) - 1 = 4.2559; constant lapse rate, below the tropopause
assumptions.steady_glide_constant_wind: one steady glide with horizontal airspeed u and sink s (u/s = L/D <= (L/D)max), constant along-track wind w (positive tailwind) with w >= -u, no vertical air motion
assumptions.daily_energy_conservation: eps dm = a I - (R + Act + s a I) over a day with every cost listed (routine, activity, SDA as a fraction s of digestible energy, Bihun et al. 2024: 0.06 in walleye); excretory losses inside a

constraints.rule: eliminated when the committed intervals for k and mu are disjoint; consistent when they overlap

kernelChecked: A neutral absorbing chain on {0..M} copies (stochastic, mean-preserving, both ends absorbing, positive one-step escape from every interior state) fixes a mutant with probability i/M, with an explicit geometric error bound at every finite time t.
The Wright-Fisher binomial kernel is such a chain (row sums, mean preservation and absorption proved from Bernstein polynomial identities).
With u = 1/M the defined substitution rate M * mu * u equals mu, also in the diploid 2N form and as the t -> infinity limit.
assumed: Strict neutrality of the mutations.
Constant population size and Wright-Fisher reproduction (non-overlapping generations, multinomial sampling).

Independent fates of mutants: the substitution rate is DEFINED, as in Kimura 1968, as (new mutants per generation) x (fixation probability of one mutant). Interference between lineages is excluded by that definition, not proved absent.
The mutation rate mu per copy per generation is a free parameter; nothing here measures it.
